newsitem.title: USA: FAA approves 'clean' aircraft de-icing system.
newsitem.headline: FAA approves 'clean' aircraft de-icing system.

text.p: An innovative carwash-like de-icing system that does not contaminate the environment was approved by the Federal Aviation Administration Wednesday for use on business and general aviation aircraft.
Conventional de-icing systems spray the chemical glycol on the plane to wash off snow and ice, often sending hundreds of gallons of the used chemical down drains and into nearby fields and streams.
The FAA said the new system, developed by Process Technologies Inc., of Orchard Park, New York, in conjunction with the agency, operates like a car wash.

A plane with snow or ice on it enters one end of a de-icing structure, is washed by infrared heat as it is pushed or pulled through, and leaves the building "clean," or free of contamination, the agency said.
In some cases the plane might need anti-icing fluids applied, if dictated by the weather, the FAA said.
With FAA approval, the system, known as InfraTekd, may be used a part of winter operations at airports."

The first system was installed at Greater Buffalo, New York, international airport as part of a joint venture by Process Technologies and Prior Aviation Services, which handles general aviation at the airport.
